You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Assuming “rich visitor” means the visitor who spent the most in total:

```sql
SELECT 
    v.ID,
    v.Name,
    v.Level_of_membership,
    v.Age,
    SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi
    ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY 
    v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
look for the visitor who bought the most tickets in one go

```sql
SELECT
    v.ID,
    v.Name,
    v.Level_of_membership,
    v.Age,
    vi.Num_of_Ticket,
    vi.Total_spent,
    m.Name AS Museum_Name
FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi
    ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
JOIN museum AS m
    ON vi.Museum_ID = m.Museum_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
the focus is on the visitor who bought the most tickets at once

```sql
SELECT
    v.ID,
    v.Name,
    v.Level_of_membership,
    v.Age,
    vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_bought_at_once,
    vi.Total_spent,
    m.Name AS Museum_Name
FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi
    ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
JOIN museum AS m
    ON vi.Museum_ID = m.Museum_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (
    SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket)
    FROM visit
);
```
I want to get the visitor's name along with their details.

```sql
SELECT
    v.Name AS visitor_name,
    v.ID,
    v.Level_of_membership,
    v.Age,
    vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_bought_at_once,
    vi.Total_spent,
    m.Name AS museum_name
FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi
    ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
JOIN museum AS m
    ON vi.Museum_ID = m.Museum_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (
    SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket)
    FROM visit
);
```

```sql

    v.Name AS visitor_name,
    v.Age AS visitor_age,
    v.ID,
    v.Level_of_membership,
    vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_bought_at_once,

FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi

JOIN museum AS m
    ON vi.Museum_ID = m.Museum_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (
    SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket)
    FROM visit
```
